skill.name: chrome-devtools-debugging
skill.description: Debug web applications through Chrome DevTools MCP using console inspection, network analysis, performance traces, JavaScript evaluation, and authenticated browser sessions.
skill.summary: Investigate browser errors, requests, performance, and page state through Chrome DevTools MCP.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, reserved example URLs, localhost endpoints, and a normal Python import. The guides expose authenticated browser data, enable remote debugging on logged-in sessions, and recommend an unpinned NPM package. Publication should require version pinning and clear browser isolation and secret-handling safeguards.

remediation.issue: Examples print authentication storage, cookies, tokens, headers, and request bodies without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad dumps with targeted checks, redact credential values by default, and warn users before sensitive data enters logs or model context.

remediation.issue: The workflow enables remote debugging against an authenticated Chrome session without isolation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dedicated temporary browser profile, keep the endpoint on loopback, close it after use, and avoid production accounts.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting recommends executing chrome-devtools-mcp through the mutable latest NPM tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and integrity metadata instead of using the latest tag.

content.user_title: Debug Web Applications with Chrome DevTools
content.value_statement: Browser failures are difficult to diagnose when console, network, and performance evidence is scattered. This skill guides focused Chrome DevTools MCP investigations.
actual_capabilities: Inspect console errors, warnings, messages, arguments, and stack traces.
List browser requests and inspect request, response, header, body, status, and timing details.
Record performance traces and analyze available insight sets.
Evaluate JavaScript expressions within the selected browser page.
Navigate pages, manage tabs, reload content, and wait for visible text.
limitations: Chrome must expose a remote debugging endpoint, and the required MCP wrappers must be installed.
Console, storage, cookies, headers, and response bodies can contain credentials or personal data.
The skill does not provide screenshots, form filling, or general browser automation.
Server-side causes remain unavailable unless browser evidence reveals them.

use_cases.title: Resolve Frontend Runtime Failures
use_cases.description: Correlate console exceptions, stack traces, and application state to identify the first actionable browser error.

use_cases.title: Validate Login and API Flows
use_cases.description: Inspect failed requests, status codes, timing, and redacted authentication signals during a controlled test session.

use_cases.title: Investigate Slow Page Loads
use_cases.description: Capture a performance trace and compare slow requests, blocking resources, and available DevTools insights.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Console Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect to the current Chrome tab. List errors and warnings from the latest page load. Group duplicates and explain the likely first cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner investigation of a broken page

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed API Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Find failed XHR and fetch requests for [workflow]. Inspect the relevant status, timing, and redacted response details. Correlate them with console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Page Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Record a fresh page-load trace for [page]. Identify slow requests and blocking resources. Rank the three highest-impact findings with supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate an Authenticated Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the authenticated failure on [page]. Use a dedicated test profile. Correlate console errors, failed requests, timing, and page state. Redact credentials and personal data. Explain the root-cause hypothesis and remaining evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-signal debugging in a controlled session

output_examples.input: Find why checkout fails after the user submits payment.
output: Primary failure: the payment request returns status 400 after 842 milliseconds.
Console correlation: the submission handler reports a missing billing postal code.
Next check: verify the client payload mapping for the postal code field.

output_examples.input: Explain why the dashboard loads slowly.
output: Largest delay: the analytics request blocks completion for 2.4 seconds.
Render impact: two scripts load before the main content becomes interactive.
Priority: defer analytics and review the larger script dependency.

output_examples.input: Check why a test account loses its session after refresh.
output_examples.output: The refresh request returns unauthorized while the expected session indicator is absent. Credential values were redacted from the report.

best_practices: Use a dedicated temporary Chrome profile and test account for authenticated debugging.
Start with narrow filters, then correlate console, network, and performance evidence by time and request.
Redact cookies, tokens, authorization headers, personal data, and sensitive response bodies before reporting results.
anti_patterns: Do not print complete browser storage, cookies, headers, or response bodies from real user sessions.
Do not expose the remote debugging endpoint beyond loopback or leave it running after the investigation.
Do not evaluate unreviewed scripts or execute mutable package versions in a trusted environment.

faq.question: What setup does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Chrome remote debugging and the Chrome DevTools MCP wrappers. Use a dedicated profile and keep the endpoint on loopback.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots or fill forms?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on console, network, performance, JavaScript evaluation, and limited navigation.

faq.question: Can it debug authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: Yes, but authenticated pages contain sensitive data. Use a test account, isolate the browser profile, and redact credentials.

faq.question: Can the skill change the active page?
faq.answer: Yes. Navigation and JavaScript evaluation can change page state, so use read-only expressions when possible.

faq.question: Can it diagnose server-side failures?
faq.answer: It can report browser-visible status, headers, timing, and response evidence. It cannot inspect server internals without additional access.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
